To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deletion of both the Zfhx3 and Pten genes promotes prostate cancer progression in the mouse.

the additive effect of Zfhx 3/Atbf 1 and Pten deletion on mouse prostatic tumorigensis is due to an increase in cell proliferation, a decrease in the smooth muscle layer, and an increase in apoptotic cells.

deletion of both the Zfhx3 (Atbf1)/Atbf1 genes and Pten gene in mouse prostate epithelium promotes the development of prostate neoplastic lesions, including high-grade mPIN or early prostatic carcinoma, by accelerating the activation of Akt- and Erk1/ 2-mediated signaling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a mouse model for the simultaneous deletion of ZfhX3/AtbfI and PTEN genes in the prostatic epithelium and the histological and molecular characterization of the resulting prostate tumors.
the additive effects of the ZFHX3 and PTEN genes in the development of prostate cancer and the progression to advanced disease.
the additive effect of Zfhx1/Atbf1 deletion together with Pten deletion on mouse prostatic tumorigenicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZFHX3 and PTEN deletional inactivation together promote prostate neoplasias.
ZFHX3 and PTEN are both tumor suppressors in the mouse prostate and are required for the maintenance of normal prostate epithelial homeostasis.
ZFHX3 and PTEN are tumor suppressor genes for prostate cancer and that the deletion of both genes is required to accelerate prostatic tumorigenic processes in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZFHX3 and PTEN act in concert to suppress the development and progression to prostate cancer.
ZFHX3 and PTEN deletional events in the prostate are not independent but synergize with each other in the progression to prostate cancer.

deletion of the Zfhx3 / Atbf1 gene together with deletion of the Pten gene in mouse prostatic cells causes a more aggressive form of prostate neoplastic lesions than that by deletion of the Ptn gene alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ZFHX3 and PTEN genes are tumor suppressors in the mouse prostate.
the loss of both genes is more effective in promoting prostate tumorigenesis than the loss of either one alone.
ZFHX3 is a tumor suppressor in mouse prostate and that its deletion together with PTEn deletion facilitates the progression of prostate neoplaisa.
